description: TRUST-569 context-consumption probe. Two LIVE turns about the SAME node: turn 1 forces a real node/docs lookup, turn 2 asks a related follow-up that turn 1's fetched definition already answers. Forced antecedent: re-verifying its own prior research is a plausible agent behaviour, so a redundant second lookup is a real miss rather than a formality. Graded on process, not on a workflow — nothing is built. Note on the token expectations: input tokens necessarily GROW turn over turn (history accumulates), so the honest signals are tool calls, output size, and cache reads — never 'turn 2 costs less than turn 1'. The cache expectation assumes a provider that reports cache usage (Anthropic does); it is worded so a provider that reports none does not red out.

conversation.text: I'm using the Notion node to list pages from a database. What credential type does it need, and does it paginate automatically if the database has thousands of pages?
For that same Notion node — can I filter which pages come back by a property value, or do I have to fetch everything and filter downstream myself?

processExpectations: Turn 2 does not call a node type-definition or documentation tool for the Notion node again — turn 1 already retrieved that node's details, and the follow-up is answerable from them.
Turn 2's output tokens stay modest next to turn 1's: it answers a narrow follow-up about filtering, it does not re-explain the node from scratch.

If the run reports cache reads at all, turn 2's cached input is a large share of its total input — it replays turn 1's prefix from cache rather than paying for it again. A turn 2 with large input and zero cached tokens is the regression this checks for.
Answers the filtering question directly instead of asking the user to restate which node or which database they mean.
